subject: The patch is named as the deliverable, never defined, and would drop half the work if produced
recordedOccasion: after the owner asked why six revisions were written straight into the checkout.
severity: F1 is high -- the rule was missed across six revisions by a session that had read it. F3 is high and independent: following the rule literally produces a patch that silently omits every new file.
scope: session management. The fix is a defined artifact, a named actor, and a guard.
read: git status and git diff --name-only over Revision 231's change set

findings.statement: A session composed correctly and then copied into the checkout six times, and never once produced a patch
Section 6 names the patch as the deliverable and never says how to produce one, where it goes, or who applies it
findings.sectionHeading: F2 -- the deliverable has no definition

findings.statement: git diff in a session copy omits every untracked file, so the prescribed patch would have carried 9 of 14 paths
findings.sectionHeading: F3 -- the prescribed patch would have dropped five of fourteen paths

findings.statement: Nothing detects a write into the owner's checkout, and the signal that used to exist was removed by 0038

edges.why: the rule cannot be followed until the artifact it names is defined
how a patch is produced and what it must carry are one answer

indexNotes: A session's account of its own failure. Offered to be checked, not believed
